articles.author: Megan, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
 
Action required
  
You may have recently been informed by Stripe that an update was required to comply with EU regulations for co-badged cards.

New regulations specify that, in the EEA, businesses handling co-branded cards are required to offer customers the option to choose their preferred network during checkout.
Rest assured, we have made the necessary updates to ensure that your guest payments are compliant with this regulation. As such, when a cardholder is using a cobadged Cartes Bancaires to pay on a Smily payment page, they are now required to select their preferred network.

Note: if you use Stripe, there are two requirements to accept Cartes Bancaires payments:
Firstly you need to enable this option in your Payment Gateway settings on Smily.


Secondly, you may need update your payment methods in your Stripe settings to be able to accept Cartes Bancaires payments. 


For more information, check out our dedicated manual article.
articles.title: Payment processing with Cartes Bancaires

articles.author: Megan, Product Manager
articles.description:
Improvement
  
Last month, we revamped the instant booking flow, and now Phase 2 is here! The new design for the payment page has launched, offering an even smoother experience when clients receive a payment link for their booking.
We know the payment process is crucial—it’s where trust is sealed. While the old design worked, it wasn’t as streamlined as it could be.
Now, with a clean, intuitive layout, the new payment page simplifies the process, making transactions faster, easier, and more transparent.
articles.title: Payment Page Redesign - Phase 2

New!
  

We are thrilled to introduce Task management v2, a groundbreaking upgrade designed to streamline your operations and elevate your management experience. This update brings powerful new features to enhance efficiency and simplify your workflow.
What's new in task management v2?
Manual task creation

Retroactive template application

Bulk edit capability
Save time by selecting and editing multiple tasks simultaneously. Update details quickly and efficiently across numerou…

articles.author: Gwenn, Designer
articles.description:
New!
  
We are thrilled to announce an exciting update to Smily! Over the past months, we have listened to your feedback and dedicated our efforts to improving the visual experience of our platform. Today, we are pleased to introduce a refreshed color palette that enhances Smily's overall quality and usability.
Why the change?
Our goal with this design refresh is to make Smily more accessible, readable, and user-friendly.
Accessibility improvements: We have corrected contrast issues to ensure that Smily meets accessibility standards, making it easier for everyone to use.
Enhanced readability: The new color palette is designed to be lighter, enhancing text readability and reducing eye strain, particularly for power users like property managers who spend extended hours on the platform.
Modern look and feel: The refreshed colors give Smily a contemporary and appealing look, which will enhance your overall experience and satisfaction.
Next steps: 
This design refresh is just the beginning. While we’ve made significant progress, we are still in the process of migrating a few legacy interfaces to our newer system, so you can expect continued improvements in the coming months.
Thank You
Best regards,
Gwenn
Designer @ Smily
articles.title: Exciting Design Refresh: Enhancing Smily’s Look and Feel!

articles.author: Megan, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
We’re excited to share a small but powerful update! You can now configure the automated payment notification emails sent to your guests directly from your General Settings.
These notifications are activated by default, but you now have the flexibility to deactivate them whenever you choose. This means more control over how and when your guests receive updates—tailored to fit your needs.
Head over to your General Settings today to adjust your payment notification preferences! 

Should you need any assistance, we’re always here to help.
articles.title: New! Manage Guest Payment Notifications from Settings

Resolved - On September 25, 2024 from 14:31 UTC to 15:06 UTC the Git Operations service experienced a degradation, leading to 1,381,993 failed git operations. The overall error rate during this period was 4.2%, with a peak error rate of 12.5%. 
The root cause was traced to a bug in a build script for a component that runs on the file servers that host git repository data. The build script incurred an error that did not cause the overall build process to fail, resulting in a faulty set of artifacts being deployed to production.
To mitigate the impact, we rolled back the affecting deployment.  
To prevent further occurrences of this cause in the future, we will be addressing the underlying cause of the ignored build failure and improving metrics and alerting for the resulting production failure scenarios.

Sep 16, 22:08 UTC
Resolved - On September 16, 2024, between 21:11 UTC and 22:20 UTC, Actions and Pages services were degraded. Customers who deploy Pages from a source branch experienced delayed runs. Approximately 1,100 runs were delayed long enough to get marked as abandoned. The runs that weren't abandoned completed successfully after we recovered from the incident. Actions jobs experienced average delays of 23 minutes, with some jobs experiencing delays as high as 45 minutes. During the course of the incident, 17% of runs were delayed by more than 5 minutes. At peak, as many as 80% of runs experienced delays exceeding 5 minutes. The root cause was a misconfiguration in the service that manages runner connections, which caused CPU throttling and led to a performance degradation in that service.
We mitigated the incident by diverting runner connections away from the misconfigured nodes. We are working to improve our internal monitoring and alerting to reduce our time to detection and mitigation of issues like this one in the future.

Resolved - On September 16, 2024, between 13:24 UTC and 14:28 UTC, the Git Operations service experienced a degradation, leading to intermittent SSH connection drops. The overall SSH error rate during this period was 0.0005%, with a peak error rate of 0.3%.
The root cause was traced to a regression in the service reload mechanism, which resulted in SSH hosts dropping connections on an hourly basis. As SSH hosts were rebooted for routine security updates, the issue progressively affected more hosts.
To mitigate the impact, we removed the affected hosts from production traffic. The SSH regression has since been identified and resolved, with all SSH hosts fully restored. Additionally, we have implemented new monitoring to alert us of any SSH connection refusals moving forward.

Sep 13, 07:13 UTC
Resolved - On Sep 13, 2024, between 05:03 UTC and 07:13 UTC, the Webhooks and Actions services were degraded resulting in some customers experiencing delayed processing of Webhooks and Actions Runs. 0.5% of Webhook deliveries were delayed more than 2 minutes during the incident. 15% of Actions Runs started between 05:03 and 05:24 UTC saw run start delays or failures. At 05:24 UTC, we implemented a mitigation to shift traffic to healthy infrastructure and new Actions Runs resumed normal operations. During the rest of the incident window, Actions runs started before 05:24 UTC continued to see delays publishing logs or job results.  No Actions runs or Webhook deliveries were lost, only delayed.
We mitigated the incident by immediately shifting traffic to a healthy cluster while investigating. The incident was caused by an erroneous configuration change on our eventing platform. A permanent fix was deployed at 06:22 UTC after which services began to recover and burn down their backed up queues, with full recovery by 07:13 UTC.
We are working to reduce our time to detection and develop test automation to prevent issues like this one in the future.

Resolved - Between August 27, 2024, 15:52 UTC and September 5, 2024, 17:26 UTC the GitHub Connect service was degraded. This specifically impacted GHES customers who were enabling GitHub Connect for the first time on a GHES instance. Previously enabled GitHub Connect GHES instances were not impacted by this issue.
Customers experiencing this issue would have received a 404 response during GitHub Connect enablement and subsequent messages about a failure to connect. This was due to a recent change in configuration to GitHub Connect which has since been rolled back. 
Subsequent enablement failures on re-attempts were caused by data corruption which has been remediated. Customers should now be able to enable GitHub Connect successfully.
To reduce our time to detection and mitigation of such issues in the future, we are working to improve observability of GitHub Connect failures. We are also making efforts to prevent future misconfiguration of GitHub Connect.

articles.description:
Issue summary: 
On September 23, 2024 from 12:11 AM PDT to 9:04 AM PDT, some users may have experienced issues uploading to or deleting files in Slack. 

A backend job responsible for file management became overwhelmed, causing an unusual spike in error rates that affected the ability for users to manage their files.

We temporarily paused the job to allow pending items to finish processing. During this time, we also released an update to the backend logic to improve processing efficiency. Once the error rates normalized and the job returned to a stable state, we resumed the process, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble uploading files to Slack

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
From September 11th, 2024 at 4:30 PM PDT to September 13th 4:00 PM PDT, some users experienced loading issues with items such as user names, avatars, channel names and their Slack Status.

We found the issue was caused by a Workflow Migrations job which flooded the real-time service with events and created a large number of bot users.

We initiated a backend cache refresh which resolved the issue for all impacted users, and the issue is now completely resolved.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble updating user status and profile photos

articles.description:
Issue summary:

From September 5, 2024 at 2:50 PM PDT to September 8, 2024 at 10 PM PDT, some customers using Enterprise Key Management (EKM) were unable to search for recently created messages. 

We traced this issue back to a recent code change which we discovered was creating indexing errors for EKM customers when they used the search function. We then reverted the problematic code change and ran a reindexing script to make the missing messages searchable again, which resolved the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Search issues for Enterprise Grid users with Enterprise Key Management (EKM) enabled.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On September 9, 2024, between 11:45 AM PDT and 1:15 PM PDT, users experienced loading issues with Workflow Builder encountering a blank page or a "Something went wrong" error while creating, editing or duplicating workflows.

We determined that a background data maintenance task caused a lag which had a cascading effect on workflow related elements, creating the issues users were experiencing. We paused this task, reducing the lag, which restored functionality for users. 

Note: This summary has been updated to better reflect the root cause and mitigation actions taken by Slack during this incident.
articles.title: Incident: Users are unable to create or edit workflows

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On Friday, September 6, 2024, between 8:00 AM PDT and 10:20 AM PDT, users could not change their availability between active and away using the desktop or browser versions of Slack.

We traced the issue to a recent code change related to updating a user's availability in our databases. Rolling back this change resolved the issue for all users.

We'll continue to implement process improvements from our review to help reduce the likelihood of this occurring in the future.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with availability status

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On August 27, 2024, from 3:16 PM PDT to 4:09 PM PDT, a change in the backend Slack web service caused the Android app to fail to boot when connecting to Slack servers.

The problems were detected by Slack internally. We rolled back a deploy to mitigate the issue for customers, resolving the issue at hand.

We apologize for any disruption this caused our Android app users.
articles.title: Incident: Users on Android experiencing crashes

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From August 27, 2024, at around 8:17 PM PDT until August 28, 2024, around 1:39 PM PDT, some Android users experienced performance issues while trying to use mentions.

We rolled back a feature flag related to the message composer on Android. This change unexpectedly introduced an error in backend logic when users attempted a mention, causing the UI to become overwhelmed and unresponsive. We identified the cause and re-enabled the feature, gradually rolling it out to users and resolving the issue for those affected.

We also determined that the app crash issue mentioned in our updates was unrelated to the performance issues. You can review our summary of that incident here: https://slack-status.com/2024-08/459426ecb123c558. We apologize for any confusion.
articles.title: Incident: A small number of users experiencing lagging behavior when using mentions on Android
